data.narrative:
Mimic Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $16M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of nine private firms and one public entity within Robotics & Manufacturing, including peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation tool here. Using total capital raised as a proxy for seed-stage value, the analysis applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier—standard for progression from seed to Series A—yielding an implied valuation of $40M. The peer-median approach is not applicable; while ten same-sector comparables exist, the narrow filter for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier peers returned insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to support meaningful cross-sectional analysis. A broad all-sector median would introduce material bias.

The triangulated valuation range is $34M to $46M, with a median point of $40M. This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of single-method analysis. Key sensitivities include the assumed step-up multiplier (which can vary by market conditions and investor appetite) and the proxy assumption that total raised approximates seed-stage post-money value. Given the limited peer data and reliance on a single method, this valuation should be updated as additional stage-comparable transactions materialize or when the company reports explicit fundraising terms.
